limitations: The prepared cotton-fabric labels in Table 1 link the own TG and measured LOI tables. Untreated A, silica-only B, silica–KH570 C and silica–gelatin E are excluded as reuse-sensitive observations; the hold is sample-specific. The TG method states a 30–700 °C scan, while Figure 6 shows traces extending to the 800 °C axis endpoint; canonical scan end is left blank. Table 4 reports generic residue without an assigned temperature, so no residue temperature is inferred. Gelatin D has a dash for residue, which is not converted to zero. The conclusion gives a broad 23.5–25.2 LOI range while discussing the ternary treatment; Table 5 assigns 23.5 to E and 25.2 to F, and the abstract independently repeats F maximum 25.2. The table value is retained with that range wording disclosed. Abstract and surface discussion refer to impregnation/baking, but preparation section 1.2.3 specifies ventilation drying without a bake temperature or time; no cure is invented. The XPS prose loosely includes D among silicon-bearing groups, while Table 1 identifies D as gelatin and Table 3 gives D no silicon value; no silica is added to D by inference. TG flow, aliquot mass, pan, handling and replication, and LOI dimensions, replication and uncertainty are unreported. Table 5 mass gains are grams; no percentage add-on is calculated. No durability-washed pair or graph-derived metric is used.
source_LOI_conclusion_range_raw: 23.5–25.2 in conclusion describing SiO2–KH570–gelatin; Table 5 separates E 23.5 and F 25.2
composition: Cotton fabric finished with 5.0 wt% aqueous gelatin; retained add-on percentage unreported
treatment_method: Aqueous gelatin mixture D contained 5.0 wt% gelatin. Cotton greige fabric from Nanjing Qicaimei Textile Co. was submerged in boiling deionized water for 5 min, repeatedly rinsed with deionized water until no yellow turbid liquid remained, and naturally air-dried. A small unspecified amount of JFC-1 penetrant was added to the finishing liquid. Cut cotton fabric was fully immersed at room temperature for 2 h and removed for ventilation drying. No post-treatment rinse, defined baking conditions or durability washing is reported.
washing_state: Preparative boil/rinse before coating; no post-treatment or durability wash assigned
pairing_evidence: Table 1 defines D as gelatin-finished cotton. Table 4 gives D T5 287.2 °C and maximum-rate temperature 342.9 °C; Table 5 gives D LOI 21.8. Both tests apply to the same initial finished fabric.

composition: Cotton fabric finished with silica sol/KH570 hydrolysate/5.0 wt% aqueous gelatin at 2.0:1.0:1.0 by volume; retained add-on percentage unreported
treatment_method: Silica sol was prepared with TEOS:ethanol molar ratio 1.0:1.3, dropwise HCl hydrolysis liquid at pH 5.0–6.0 and 60 °C for 3 h, then an unspecified amount of NaOH solution adjusted pH to approximately 7.0. KH570 hydrolysate contained KH570/ethanol/deionized water 20.0/72.0/8.0 vol% and was mixed and hydrolyzed at room temperature. Silica sol, KH570 hydrolysate and 5.0 wt% aqueous gelatin were combined in source-reported volume ratio 2.0:1.0:1.0, stirred and aged for 2 h. Quantities of HCl/water and NaOH are unreported. Cotton greige fabric from Nanjing Qicaimei Textile Co. was submerged in boiling deionized water for 5 min, repeatedly rinsed with deionized water until no yellow turbid liquid remained, and naturally air-dried. A small unspecified amount of JFC-1 penetrant was added to the finishing liquid. Cut cotton fabric was fully immersed at room temperature for 2 h and removed for ventilation drying. No post-treatment rinse, defined baking conditions or durability washing is reported.
